label: first copy-phase feedback of a leading o (step L+1, input o) in sequences of length >= 6
explanation: Fires only at the step right after <DEL> plus one (recall_idx 1, t = L+1), and only when the input there is o, meaning the first original token was o and the model fed its own first output back in. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or at any other copy position. Within that context it needs longer sequences: there is none at L <= 5, it is weak or patchy at L = 6, and it is nearly always on at L >= 7 (precision about 1.0). Magnitude grows with L. L = 6 accounts for 2% of activation mass and L = 9 for 43%. Neither the token being output nor later tokens modulate it. About 1% of activations are weak hits where the first token is a different token (mostly 2).

issues: All structural claims check out on dev. The feature fires only in the copy phase, only at recall_idx 1, and never at L <= 5. 99.9% of activation mass has in_tok o. Mass share by L is 0.021 / 0.197 / 0.348 / 0.434 for L = 6..9.
Test score of the original predicate is reproduced: P 0.880, R 0.984, F1 0.929, mass recall 0.999. With L >= 7: P 0.9999, R 0.842, F1 0.914.

The only systematic gap is L = 6, where precision is about 0.54 (1315 test false positives, all at step 7, L = 6). It looks like a graded threshold region, not a separate class. No single variable cleanly splits firing from non-firing there: correct, in_count, out_tok type and n_digits all leave precision at about 0.5. Some content does shift it: orig(1) == o gives 0.92 and a digit at orig(5) gives 0.73, while o at orig(5) gives 0.23. These L = 6 activations are weak (2% of mass).
Missed activations are 155 test steps holding 0.1% of mass, all weak (<= 0.11 of max). They are at recall_idx 1 with first token 2, z, m, r and so on, which is scattered noise.
Small overstatement: 'mostly 2' for non-o hits is only about half of them (73 of about 125 on dev).
